title: DateTimePicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.DatePickerDialog with androidx.compose.material3.DatePicker, and androidx.compose.material3.TimePickerDialog with androidx.compose.material3.TimePicker or androidx.compose.material3.TimeInput and androidx.compose.material3.rememberTimePickerState, inside MonarchFormField
summary: A date and a wall-clock time chosen with the Material 3 date picker and time picker, each opened in its own dialog from a button in one MonarchFormField row, with the time zone shown beside them as a separate label or control. Monarch ships nothing; the theme styles both pickers.
whenToUse: For one moment in a form that needs both a day and a time: an interview, a booking start, a reminder. Show the two buttons side by side, as Android calendar apps do, so the person can change one without the other.
whenNotToUse: For a day alone use the Material 3 DatePicker (see date-picker); for a time alone the Material 3 TimePicker or TimeInput. To pick from offered times (booking slots), use slot-picker. For a start and an end, use two of these rows or a date range picker.
api: @Composable fun DatePickerDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, confirmButton: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, dismissButton: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, …, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
@Composable fun DatePicker(state: DatePickerState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, showModeToggle: Boolean = true, …)

@Composable fun TimePickerDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, confirmButton: @Composable () -> Unit, title: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, properties: DialogProperties = DialogProperties(), dismissButton: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, modeToggleButton: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, …, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun TimePicker(state: TimePickerState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, colors: TimePickerColors = TimePickerDefaults.colors(), layoutType: TimePickerLayoutType = TimePickerDefaults.layoutType())
@Composable fun TimeInput(state: TimePickerState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, colors: TimePickerColors = TimePickerDefaults.colors())
@Composable fun rememberTimePickerState(initialHour: Int = 0, initialMinute: Int = 0, is24Hour: Boolean = is24HourFormat): TimePickerState

object TimePickerDialogDefaults { @Composable fun Title(displayMode: TimePickerDisplayMode, modifier: Modifier = Modifier); @Composable fun DisplayModeToggle(onDisplayModeChange: () -> Unit, displayMode: TimePickerDisplayMode, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) }

states.name: set
states.description: The date button shows the day in the locale's medium format and the time button the time in the person's 12- or 24-hour setting.

states.name: no date yet
states.description: The app keeps a Long? for the day and shows "Set date"; the time keeps a default (the web uses 09:00) until the person changes it.

states.name: clock face or keyboard
states.description: The time dialog's mode toggle switches between the clock face (TimePicker) and typed hours and minutes (TimeInput), validated by Material 3.

states.name: limited
states.description: Days are limited with SelectableDates and yearRange on the date picker. The time picker has no minimum or maximum: the app checks the combined value and shows errorText on MonarchFormField.

states.name: invalid
states.description: MonarchFormField shows the app's errorText under the row, for example "Choose 09:00 or later."

states.name: disabled
states.description: MonarchFormField(enabled = false) with disabled buttons; neither dialog can open.

appearance: Both dialogs use the raised surface with the extra-large corners; the selected day, the clock hand and the selected hour or minute field use the accent solid role with its on-solid text, all from MonarchTheme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes. The zone label uses the muted text role.
platformNotes: The web DateTimePicker is one field: a DatePicker plus a typed time with arrow-key steps, min and max to the minute, presets and a time zone slot, with the value as a zone-less YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm string. On Android the expected control is two buttons that open the Material 3 date and time pickers, as in Android calendar apps; the time follows the person's 12- or 24-hour system setting (rememberTimePickerState reads it) instead of the locale alone. Keep the value as the day's UTC midnight (DatePickerState.selectedDateMillis) plus hour * 60 + minute, a wall-clock value that never shifts with the device's zone; format it with a UTC formatter. The time zone is a separate slot: a label or a time zone select beside the buttons; neither picker converts between zones. The time picker has no step, minimum or maximum: round and check in the app. Presets are a MonarchMenu as in date-picker. iOS uses the SwiftUI DatePicker with .date and .hourAndMinute components in the same MonarchFormField row.
accessibility: System behavior: each dialog is a window with its own title, so TalkBack moves into it and returns to the button that opened it when it closes.
System behavior: in the clock face, hours and minutes are selectable items read with their value; in TimeInput, the hour and minute fields are text fields with their labels, and AM/PM is a toggle.
The date and time buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets whose text says the date and the time, labelled by MonarchFormField.
The time zone is plain text read after the buttons; nothing depends on color.
Font scale, right to left and the 12- or 24-hour clock are handled by Material 3.
edgeCases: selectedDateMillis is a UTC midnight: format the date and the combined value with a UTC formatter, or west of UTC it shows the previous day.
A wall-clock time that does not exist or exists twice on a daylight-saving change is not checked by either picker; resolve it when converting to an instant in the event's zone.
TimePickerState keeps the time while the dialog is closed; copy hour and minute into the app's value only on OK, so Cancel discards the change.
Both dialogs are tall; at the largest font scale on a small phone the date dialog scrolls and TimeInput fits better than the clock face.

parityExceptions.reason: the Material 3 TimePicker has no minute interval, so the web's 15-minute step cannot be set
parityExceptions.convention: the Material 3 TimePicker is the platform time control and has no minute interval; the value stays a time
